tasks.question: Scope and coordinate the evidence-led incident investigation.
notes: Current state is evidence-insufficient: no canonical records, metrics, or history are supplied yet, so no diagnosis is justified.
Scope first: determine tenant impact, request count, and whether text-only scheduled messages succeed while only file-bearing scheduled messages degrade.
Begin queries with null filters to avoid silently excluding records missing service or timestamp fields; then narrow by incident time, service=tool-executor, action/tool path, and affected tenant(s).

Prefer canonical sources: execution logs, request payload records, provider request/response envelopes, and upload/reference lifecycle records. Do not rely on derived connection/refresh views as independent proof.
Key observability comparisons: failure rate and latency for scheduled Slack sends with file descriptors vs without files; if available, compare immediate sends with the same file mechanism.

Look for mechanism evidence in payloads: exact argument nesting/path for file descriptors, whether a supported file object/link was passed, and whether tool-executor stripped or transformed file fields before provider handoff.
Check whether requests demonstrably reached Slack. If provider requests omit attachment fields, focus on internal serialization/semantics rather than demanding provider traces.

If provider requests include file-related fields and Slack accepts the schedule but later delivers only text, evaluate provider feature/semantic limitations for scheduled messages before inferring an internal regression.

Verify file-reference lifecycle timing: upload/create time, TTL/expiry, and whether the schedule execution occurs after reference invalidation. This would distinguish temporary reference expiry from argument-shape issues.
Dependency review should treat deployment timing as a hypothesis only. Seek counter-evidence such as unaffected tenants on the same version or pre/post change controls.
Useful discriminating controls: same tenant, same channel, same connection, same file source, varying only send mode (scheduled vs immediate) or attachment representation.
If no canonical telemetry exists for file serialization or downstream request contents, record that as a material telemetry gap and keep the conclusion inconclusive pending those records.

tasks.question: Using null filters first, what canonical execution/request records exist for the affected scheduled Slack sends during 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z–10:15:00Z, and for each failed example do they show: the exact serialized attachment/file argument shape submitted to tool-executor, whether a file upload/reference was present at schedule time, whether the downstream Slack scheduling request included any file-related fields, the execution status/latency by step, and the affected tenant/request count versus comparable scheduled sends without files?
notes: Canonical records in the requested window are sparse: one affected tool-executor log for cedar at 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z, request_id=req-52, showing Slack schedule accepted (status 200, message_scheduled=true) but no file outcome (file_upload_performed=false, file_link_in_body=false, delivered_file_count=0, attachment_semantics=legacy_message_formatting) [ev_dae9cefe92dc/slack-schedule-052:logs:0]. A comparison cedar request-envelope/provider-envelope record for the exact serialized attachment/file argument shape is not present in the supplied canonical evidence, nor is any canonical downstream Slack scheduling request body showing file-related fields.

The supplied canonical evidence does show a file/reference was not turned into an upload or body link at execution time for the failed example, but it does not show whether an uploaded file descriptor/reference was already present at schedule time: cedar req-52 only records file_upload_performed=false and file_link_in_body=false [ev_dae9cefe92dc/slack-schedule-052:logs:0]. The reproduce control matches that mechanism observation under sandbox conditions, with original vs corrected differing only in Slack configuration and flipping from no upload/no link/delivered_file_count=0 to upload/link/delivered_file_count=1 [ev_4584563cb3ea/slack-schedule-052:reproduce:0; ev_4584563cb3ea/slack-schedule-052:reproduce:1], but reproduce is not canonical production request telemetry.

Step-level execution status/latency is not available from canonical records: only aggregate tenant metrics are supplied. For cedar at 10:05Z there were 823 requests, 0 platform failures, queue_depth 147, p95 latency 1960 ms, and 445 business_operations_blocked [ev_42c85794c3b0/slack-schedule-052:metrics:0]. No per-step timings for schedule creation vs file handling vs downstream Slack call are present, so the requested step latency breakdown cannot be established from canonical evidence.

Observed tenant/comparison scope is limited. Affected evidence is only cedar/req-52 in canonical logs [ev_dae9cefe92dc/slack-schedule-052:logs:0]. Compared with maple at the same timestamp, tool-executor had status 200 on an unrelated read and metrics of 659 requests, 0 failures, queue_depth 0, p95 latency 160 ms [ev_edbd7e1580fb/slack-schedule-052:logs:1; ev_5b79d76b2f18/slack-schedule-052:metrics:1]. This supports tenant-local impact and backlog difference, but there is no canonical count of scheduled Slack sends with files vs scheduled Slack sends without files, so comparative affected-request counts by message type remain a telemetry gap.

tasks.question: What changed around the incident window in tool-executor or its Slack integration path—deployments, toolkit/version pins, argument serialization changes, feature flags, or connection/auth handling—and is there any contemporaneous provider-side or platform-side change affecting scheduled messages with attachments specifically, as opposed to general Slack delivery?
notes: No contemporaneous tool-executor deployment was observed in the incident window: the service-specific deployment query from 09:30Z-10:30Z returned no records, while the only deployment found was an unrelated support-dashboard release at 10:05Z. This is counter-evidence against a same-window executor rollout as the trigger, but it does not rule out an earlier configuration/version change not captured here. [ev_e5be74551969; ev_531b827f1540/slack-schedule-052:deployments:0]

Canonical execution evidence shows scheduled Slack requests succeeded at HTTP/status level but did not perform file upload or include a file link when using legacy attachment semantics: cedar request req-52 logged status 200, message_scheduled=true, file_upload_performed=false, file_link_in_body=false, delivered_file_count=0. A controlled sandbox comparison varied only Slack configuration and changed outcome from 0 delivered files to 1, again without any provider failure signal. This supports an integration-path/configuration/semantics hypothesis more than general Slack delivery failure. [ev_abac5cf7017b/slack-schedule-052:logs:0; ev_4584563cb3ea/slack-schedule-052:reproduce:0; ev_4584563cb3ea/slack-schedule-052:reproduce:1]

Observed scope is selective rather than platform-wide: cedar shows 823 requests, 0 recorded failures, but 445 business operations blocked, queue_depth 147, p95 latency 1960 ms, whereas maple on the same platform shows 659 requests, 0 failures, 0 blocked operations, queue_depth 0, p95 160 ms; maple also has an unrelated Slack read succeeding. That pattern argues against a broad Slack outage and points toward a path specific to scheduled messages with attachments for affected flows/tenants. [ev_5b79d76b2f18/slack-schedule-052:metrics:0; ev_5b79d76b2f18/slack-schedule-052:metrics:1; ev_abac5cf7017b/slack-schedule-052:logs:1]

There is no direct evidence here of a provider-side or platform-side change specific to Slack scheduled attachments: dependency records only show provider_api_reachable=true, and no canonical records were supplied for toolkit/version pins, feature flags, argument-serialization diffs, connection/auth changes, or provider changelog events. Those are material gaps, so the strongest current read is 'no observed same-window deployment/change,' not proof that no earlier configuration or semantic change occurred. [ev_c04cd0443220/slack-schedule-052:dependencies:0; ev_f09e8671d2af/slack-schedule-052:dependencies:0]

tasks.question: Which hypothesis best matches the observed failed executions: (1) scheduled attachments are not supported/are dropped by Slack scheduling semantics, (2) the attachment/file descriptor shape is being serialized incorrectly before provider handoff, or (3) the referenced uploaded file is stale/expired/unavailable by execution time; and what discriminating control cases exist (immediate send with same file descriptor, scheduled send without file, scheduled send with a freshly uploaded supported file object/link) to separate these mechanisms?

records.symptom: A similar workflow stopped following a release
records.relation: historical analogy only, not current proof

records.summary: Scheduled-message formatting attachments are not a file-upload operation.

notes: Best current match: hypothesis (1) scheduled attachment semantics, with hypothesis (2) incorrect descriptor shape/serialization still plausible because canonical payload capture is missing.
Hypothesis (3) temporary file expiry is weakest because the observed execution never shows a file upload or body link attempt, and no file lifecycle records were supplied.

hypothesis.description: The observed failed executions best match scheduled-message attachment semantics that do not perform a file upload for legacy-formatted scheduled Slack messages, so the text is scheduled successfully but the file is omitted unless it is converted to a supported link/object path.
assumptions: Observed production evidence is limited to cedar req-52 rather than a full census of all scheduled Slack sends.
The sandbox controlled comparison is verification of the changed Slack configuration variable, not independent proof of all provider behavior in production.

findings.statement: In the affected production request, Slack scheduling succeeded at the HTTP level but no file upload was performed, no file link was placed in the body, and zero files were delivered.

A controlled sandbox comparison varied only Slack configuration: the original scheduled message path delivered 0 files with no upload/link, while the corrected path delivered 1 file with upload/link enabled.
A broad Slack/provider outage is not supported here: provider API reachability was true, and another tenant had a successful unrelated Slack read during the window.

Impact appears selective to the affected flow/tenant rather than platform-wide: cedar had 445 business operations blocked with queue depth 147 and p95 latency 1960 ms, while maple had 0 blocked operations, queue depth 0, and p95 latency 160 ms.

actions: Treat scheduled Slack sends with files as a separate path: upload the file separately and include a supported link/object in the scheduled message body rather than relying on legacy attachment formatting.
Collect canonical request/serialization telemetry for scheduled sends so the outbound Slack payload shows whether file-related fields are omitted before provider handoff.

Request/retain discriminating controls for the same file source: immediate send with same descriptor, scheduled send without file, and scheduled send with a freshly uploaded supported file link/object.
missing_checks: Canonical production control comparing immediate send with the same file descriptor versus scheduled send is not present.
Canonical production control for scheduled send without file is not present.
Canonical production outbound Slack request body is missing, so omission before provider handoff is inferred from execution fields rather than directly observed.

hypothesis.description: An incorrect attachment/file descriptor shape or serialization path before provider handoff caused the scheduler to omit file handling, so the message text was scheduled but the file fields were never transformed into an upload or link.
assumptions: The controlled sandbox result could reflect corrected attachment representation rather than only provider-side scheduling semantics.
No canonical payload capture is available to distinguish wrong descriptor shape from intentionally unsupported scheduled attachment semantics.

findings.statement: The failed production execution shows no upload and no file link despite a successful scheduled message, which is consistent with attachment fields being dropped or not transformed before handoff.

Changing only Slack configuration in sandbox changed the result from omitted file handling to one delivered file, indicating a configuration/serialization-path discriminator rather than a general provider outage.
No canonical request-envelope or outbound provider payload was supplied for req-52, so the exact serialized attachment argument path and shape cannot be verified from production telemetry.

actions: Validate that scheduled Slack sends serialize the uploaded file descriptor into the supported file object/link shape rather than legacy formatting fields alone.
Capture canonical pre-handoff payloads for the failed path to confirm whether attachment fields are missing or mis-nested.
Compare the serialized argument shape between the original and corrected Slack configurations used in the controlled reproduction.
missing_checks: Canonical production payload showing the exact attachment/file descriptor shape before provider handoff is unavailable.
A canonical control with a freshly uploaded supported file object/link in production is unavailable.

hypothesis.description: The referenced uploaded file may have been stale or unavailable by scheduled execution time, causing the scheduled message to go out as text only.
assumptions: A file descriptor may have existed at schedule time even though no canonical upload/reference lifecycle records are present.

findings.statement: No canonical upload timestamp, TTL, or file-reference lifecycle record was provided, so expiry/unavailability cannot be tested directly.
The observed production request delivered zero files, but the records do not show any attempted file upload or reference resolution failure at execution time.

actions: If this path remains under investigation, verify file-reference age/TTL and whether the referenced upload still existed at scheduled execution time.
Add canonical file lifecycle telemetry so schedule-time reference creation and execution-time resolution can be compared.
missing_checks: Canonical file upload/create record and TTL for the referenced descriptor are missing.
A discriminating control using the same schedule flow with a freshly uploaded file reference in production is missing.

tasks.question: Challenge the diagnosis, evidence grounding and verification gaps.
notes: The leading diagnosis is sufficiently bounded for the observed failure: cedar req-52 shows status 200 with message_scheduled=true but file_upload_performed=false, file_link_in_body=false, delivered_file_count=0 in canonical production logs [ev_dae9cefe92dc/slack-schedule-052:logs:0].

The controlled sandbox comparison is discriminating enough to support probable cause, not mere correlation: with only Slack configuration changed, the original condition reproduces no upload/no link/0 delivered files, while the corrected condition performs upload/link and delivers 1 file [ev_4584563cb3ea/slack-schedule-052:reproduce:0; ev_4584563cb3ea/slack-schedule-052:reproduce:1].

Public reference evidence is consistent with, not sole proof of, the mechanism: scheduled-message legacy formatting attachments are not a file-upload operation [ev_4c097f357a92/slack-schedule-052:knowledge:0].

No same-window tool-executor deployment was observed, which weakens an internal rollout-trigger theory but does not prove no earlier change existed [ev_e5be74551969; ev_531b827f1540/slack-schedule-052:deployments:0].

I would clear the candidate's proposed 'missing checks' as non-blocking for diagnosis approval. Immediate-send and scheduled-no-file production controls would improve scope/coverage, but they are not required to explain the observed failed execution once the production mechanism and discriminating sandbox control already align.

Keep scope narrow in any summary: this supports probable cause for observed scheduled Slack sends using legacy attachment semantics/file descriptors like cedar req-52, not proof about every Slack scheduled send or every tenant.

tasks.question: Write the evidence-backed internal report and proposed next steps.

hypotheses.description: Most likely cause: scheduled Slack sends using legacy attachment semantics accepted and scheduled the text, but did not perform a file upload or include a supported file link/object, so the message arrived without its file. This is bounded to the observed scheduled-file path like cedar req-52, not all Slack sends.
assumptions: The sandbox controlled comparison validates the configuration discriminator but is still synthetic telemetry rather than canonical production payload capture.
Observed production scope is limited to the supplied requests and tenants, especially cedar req-52.

hypotheses.description: Alternative plausible cause: the uploaded file descriptor was serialized in an unsupported attachment/reference shape on the scheduled path, so file fields were omitted before provider handoff even though the schedule request itself succeeded.
assumptions: No canonical outbound Slack payload for req-52 was supplied, so exact argument shape cannot be verified from production telemetry.
The corrected sandbox configuration may have changed representation/serialization as well as semantics.

hypotheses.description: Less likely alternative: the referenced uploaded file had expired or become unavailable by scheduled execution time, leading to text-only delivery.
assumptions: A file reference existed at schedule time, but no canonical upload lifecycle or TTL record was provided.

recommended_actions: Use the scheduled-send path that uploads the file separately and includes a supported link/object in the scheduled Slack message body rather than relying on legacy attachment formatting. This action is proposed only and has not been executed.

Capture canonical pre-handoff and outbound Slack payload telemetry for scheduled sends so attachment/file fields can be verified before provider handoff. This action is proposed only and has not been executed.

Request discriminating comparisons for the same file source: immediate send with the same descriptor, scheduled send without a file, and scheduled send with a freshly uploaded supported file link/object. These checks are proposed only and have not been executed.
Continue monitoring tenant-selective backlog/latency on cedar while comparing against unaffected tenants such as maple to confirm scope. Monitoring is proposed only and has not been executed.
limitations: Synthetic telemetry was used for the controlled sandbox comparison; it is discriminating but not canonical production payload evidence.
No canonical outbound Slack request body or request-envelope serialization for cedar req-52 was supplied, so the exact attachment/reference shape before provider handoff is unverified.
The evidence set is sparse for production scope: canonical affected execution evidence is centered on cedar req-52, with maple serving only as an unaffected comparison tenant.
Recommended actions are proposals and have not been executed within this investigation.
